result:
If I could change the world in one way, I would eliminate the illusion of separation—the belief that we are fundamentally distinct from one another, from other species, and from the Earth itself.

This shift would dissolve the roots of greed, conflict, and exploitation, because you cannot harm what you recognize as part of yourself. Empathy would become the default, not the exception. Systems built on extraction and domination would collapse, replaced by structures that nourish life in all its forms.

It wouldn’t erase difference or conflict, but it would transform how we engage with them—no longer as battles between "us" and "them," but as tensions within a single, interconnected whole. The question would no longer be *"What can I take?"* but *"What can we become?"*

(And then, of course, I’d watch as humanity immediately found new ways to mess it up. But at least the mess would be more interesting.)
